title: Key edit detection on content hash, not filename
context: Auto-refresh of generated MADR files silently destroyed hand edits when numbering shifted. File renumbering changes filenames, so name-keyed edit checks missed moved files; the removal sweep also deleted edited files under their old names. Two silent corruption paths. Touches invariant(s): con_8460b6770f (Config/provider writers must merge idempotently into existing user files and refuse to clobber an unparseable file).
decision: Detect hand edits by file content hash (SHA16), not by filename. The manifest's `bytes` values are exactly the set of file states this system ever wrote; any on-disk generated file with a hash not in that set must be human-edited, regardless of its current name.
consequences: Hand edits survive renumbering in both write path (skipped) and removal sweep (preserved with manifest entry)
Manifest entries now carry through for edited files, so madr-edited drift keeps firing until human resolves
Plain renumbering with no edits still shuffles file names cleanly without false positives
alternatives_rejected: Name-keyed edit detection (prior approach)—breaks when renumbering shifts filenames; was the root cause
Timestamp-based detection—less reliable; doesn't distinguish generated vs hand-edited
